name: Egara-Guti
boardDescription: Lau Kata Kati 'butterfly' board (two triangles joined at a common vertex, 19 points) plus two extra lines, each running from one triangle's base to the other's through the points where the second ranks meet the triangle edges; the lines add 2 new intersection points per base, for 23 points total.
ruleNotes: Captures compulsory, by the short leap as in draughts/Alquerque, in a straight line following the board pattern; multiple captures per turn allowed. Win by capturing all enemy pieces. Stalemate loses; if no more captures are possible, the player with more pieces wins, equal counts draw.
sources: H.J.R. Murray, A History of Board-Games Other Than Chess (1952), p.71 (via Wikipedia 'Egara-guti' article)

Mats Winther, 'Indian War-games' (mats-winther.github.io/bg/indian_wg.htm) — board diagram with starting layout (verified by pixel measurement: 11 pieces per triangle, center vacant; extra lines are verticals through the 2nd-rank edge points, adding 2 base points per triangle)
Wikipedia 'Egara-guti' — Lau kata kati board + 'two lines connecting the two triangles and running through them'; 23 intersection points
J.M. Datta (1939), 'Challis-Ghutia and its degenerate variants', Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal V, pp.257-258 (cited by Wikipedia for Egara-guti)
gaps: Murray's original 1952 text not directly consulted (all located PDF mirrors returned errors/redirects); board and start data via secondary sources citing Murray
Datta (1939) paper not directly retrieved; cited second-hand via Wikipedia
Starting player not documented — sources say players choose color and who starts
